A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REFINE research work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Material can be matched across the extensive renumbering and relocation, including appendices A-D in v1 and A-E in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original image, sentiment and tabular transfer experiments, including multi-source evaluations and robustness/ablation results in Sections 4 and C.

after.justification: V2 retains original transfer experiments and adds LoRA/DANN-Gate comparisons, spatial-omics evaluations and an encoder-capacity study in Sections 5 and C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains frozen source features, a trainable residual encoder and their concatenation. Section 5.4 adds a specific adaptation: a residual spatial encoder supplies a modality absent from the frozen scGPT source model. This extends the inputs and residual branch without replacing the core algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds human lymph-node anatomical classification using SpatialGlue transcriptomes and spatial coordinates, specifically testing a modality available only during adaptation. It removes the Sim Binary and Sim Multi tabular datasets and the Gaussian feature-corruption scenario. The original image and sentiment transfer datasets remain.

E2.justification: LoRA and DANN-Gate are added to the natural-distribution-shift and CNN/transformer stress comparisons in Tables 1-2 and S1-S3. Conversely, v1's UnweightedAvg comparisons in Tables 13-14 disappear. LinearProb/LinearProbe and Distillation/Distill are retained methods despite naming changes.

E3.justification: Retained sample sizes and metrics largely match v1 Table 18 and v2 Table S6. New protocols include a spatial study spanning 1,000-3,000 labeled cells and five encoder width/depth configurations. Tabular corruption is described as random labels in v1 but 80% label flips in v2; unchanged scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds encoder-capacity ablations (Figure S3) and spatial prediction/error comparisons (Figure S2). It removes v1's fusion-depth study, scaling/inference-time analysis up to 15 sources, unweighted-averaging robustness tests and tabular feature-noise analysis. Adapter-size sensitivity and noisy/low-learning-rate multi-source analyses are retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report plus/minus uncertainty entries, graphical error bars and seed 42 for imbalance sampling. Neither specifies repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures. The new spatial results provide no additional uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds spatial and encoder-ablation results and new comparator scores; for CIFAR-10 transformer domain mismatch, DANN-Gate/LoRA reach 47.79/47.74 accuracy versus REFINE's retained 44.85 (Table S2). Clean single-source results, clean multi-source panels and several appendix results are removed. Most retained entries match after rounding, but NoTrans accuracy under CIFAR-10 transformer imbalance changes from 45.168 to 45.36 (v1 Table 11; v2 Table S2).

T1.justification: Beyond restating v1's rate implications as Corollaries 4.2-4.3, v2 introduces a target-function class, worst-case Corollary 4.4, asymptotic Proposition A.1 and their proofs, and refines Lemma B.3. Theorem 4.1 changes the density/residual assumptions and weight bound. It also omits v1 Theorem 5.1's explicit assumption that the optimal probe has norm at most one, although Appendix A.1 still invokes it.

C1.justification: V2 adds central claims that this is the first theoretical protection against negative transfer and that REFINE uniquely enables adaptation-time multimodality extension. The abstract and introduction elevate the new single-cell application to a contribution and frame the retained convergence guarantee more explicitly through target-function classes and logarithmic factors.

C2.justification: V2 introduces missing pretraining modalities as a failure mechanism and expands source-free applicability arguments, while removing v1's future-work discussion and some parameter-cost qualifications. It also strengthens performance interpretations beyond the tables: Section 5.3 claims nearly 35 points over the strongest adaptive alternative at 80% noise, although Table 2 reports Distill at 53.51 and REFINE at 56.58.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies CNN channels/layers and transformer patch sizes, dimensions and depths; these are disclosures rather than demonstrated architecture changes. Conversely, v1 Table 19's dataset-specific epoch budgets and the tabular probability-feature construction are omitted. The public repository link is replaced by an anonymized-supplement statement and a promise of later public release.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix E substantially expand positioning relative to LoRA, DANN-Gate, affine model transformation, deep transfer learning and multimodal learning. SAFEW, already cited in v1, receives a substantive comparison. V2 adds biological/multimodal references and removes the dedicated data-augmentation discussion and several associated citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, related work and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Theory moves before experiments, natural distribution shift precedes controlled corruption, multi-source experiments move to the appendix, and the conclusion is removed. Ethics/reproducibility statements and a further-related-work appendix are added.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR layout and extensively reorganizes displays: v1 Tables 4-5 merge into Table 1, and stress tables are regrouped into Table 2 and S1-S3. Multi-source plots move to Figure S1 with the clean row removed. Spatial and encoder-capacity figures are added, several old displays disappear, and the unchanged schematic and adapter-size plots are relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens comparator coverage and adds a relevant spatial-modality application and explicit safety analyses. However, Theorem 4.1 omits a condition that Appendix A.1 still requires, and new performance summaries conflict with the tables. Removing clean-data/robustness analyses, dataset-specific epoch information and the public code link also offsets gains in architecture disclosure. These substantive additions and unresolved validity/reporting losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
